U2: Python processor (investigate integration approach)
U3: R processor (investigate integration approach)
U4: Hive sink
U5: Upgrade Spring Core to 4.1.1

- ACL implementation using Spring Security ACL module
- Configuration via existing Spring configuration mechanism

- Working on Spring XD codebase
- Spring Core 4.1.1 is the target version
- Single developer with good knowledge of Spring ecosystem
- Standard 8-hour workday
- Includes design, implementation, unit testing, and integration testing
- Documentation updates included

technical_and_design_decisions: Python integration will be implemented using a subprocess approach (stdin/stdout) rather than JNI/Jep, because it is simpler, more portable, and avoids native library dependencies.

R integration will be implemented using Renjin (JVM-based R interpreter) rather than rJava, because Renjin runs on the JVM without requiring native R installation and fits the Spring XD deployment model better.
Hive sink will use the Hive JDBC driver (HiveServer2) for writing data, as it is the standard supported way to integrate with Hive and avoids coupling to a specific Hive version.
SSL/HTTPS and Basic authentication will be implemented using standard Servlet container configuration (Tomcat/Netty) plus Spring Security configuration files.
ACLs for DSL Shell and Admin UI will be implemented using Spring Security's ACL module, sharing a common ACL service and per-resource permission definitions.
Entity-level security definitions (U6) will leverage Spring Security method-level security with @PreAuthorize annotations and a centralized permission model.
Spring Core 4.1.1 upgrade will be performed in a dedicated branch, with dependency tree analysis and compatibility fixes for SpEL, etc.
assumptions: A single experienced developer familiar with the Spring ecosystem performs all the work.
Estimates include design, implementation, unit tests, and basic integration testing for each activity.
Standard 8-hour work day, effort expressed in work-hours.
Spring XD source code is available and can be built locally.
Python 3.x and R runtimes are available on developer/test machines for testing the respective processors.
Hive and a Hadoop test environment (or at least HiveServer2) are available for Hive sink development and testing.
U6, U7, and U8 are related and partially share infrastructure (security model, ACL tables), so some effort is reused but each user story is still implemented as a distinct deliverable.
Documentation updates are limited to inline Javadoc and a short release-notes entry; no separate user guide writing is included beyond that.
The Spring Core 4.1.1 upgrade (U5) is treated as a precondition that other work may depend on, so it is scheduled early in the WBS.
No major refactoring of existing processors/sinks beyond what is required by the listed user stories.

activities.activity_description: Review all eight user stories, identify shared components (security/ACL infrastructure), produce a high-level design document and update the WBS.
Update Spring Core dependency to 4.1.1 milestone, fix any breaking changes, address compiled SpEL adjustments, and verify the build/tests still pass.

activities.activity_name: Implement SSL/HTTPS and Basic authentication for admin endpoints (U1)
activities.activity_description: Add configuration options (properties/YAML) for enabling HTTPS and Basic auth on admin endpoints; wire Spring Security HTTP configuration; document the new options.
Investigate integration options, design a Python processor module using stdin/stdout subprocess, implement payload marshaling, write unit tests, and verify end-to-end with a sample stream.
Investigate R integration options, choose Renjin, design and implement the R processor with payload marshaling, write unit tests, and verify end-to-end with a sample stream.
Investigate Hive connectivity options, implement a Hive sink using the HiveServer2 JDBC driver, support configurable table/partition options, add unit and integration tests.

activities.activity_name: Implement entity-level security definitions for REST API (U6)
activities.activity_description: Define a security model that allows per-entity (REST API) group/role access policies; implement using Spring Security method-level security and a centralized permission registry; add tests.
Add ACL configuration support for DSL Shell commands (create/destroy/view streams), reuse shared ACL infrastructure, default to open access when no ACL is configured; add tests.
Add ACL configuration support for Admin UI actions (create/destroy/view streams), reuse shared ACL infrastructure, default to open access when no ACL is configured; add tests.
Run end-to-end tests combining new processors/sinks with the security/ACL features and the Spring Core 4.1.1 upgrade; fix issues found.
Update Javadoc, configuration reference, and add a short release-notes entry covering the new features and the Spring Core 4.1.1 upgrade.
